title: EU Vulnerability Database: latest, exploited and recently updated (ENISA EUVD)

provenance.by: sources/euvd/collect.mjs (code, no model; run by data.b@PrompTugal.dinis)
provenance.terms: EUVD's API page says no authentication is needed and sets limits of 100 records a request; the EUVD site's footer links ENISA's legal notice, 1.2: reproduction of material on ENISA's website is authorised if the source is acknowledged, unless stated otherwise. robots.txt of euvd.enisa.europa.eu: all agents, nothing disallowed; euvdservices.enisa.europa.eu (the API host) has no robots.txt (404). We name ENISA and the EUVD as the source. EUVD has no separate data licence page that we found: reuse rests on the ENISA legal notice (not reviewed by a person).
provenance.robots: https://euvd.enisa.europa.eu/robots.txt (User-agent *, empty Disallow); euvdservices.enisa.europa.eu/robots.txt answered 404 (no rules)

about: Vulnerabilities in the EU Vulnerability Database (EUVD, run by ENISA) that were published or updated in the 24 hours before the read, plus EUVD's own latest and exploited lists: each with its EUVD identifier, CVE aliases, dates, CVSS base score and version, a severity band (ours, from the score by the standard CVSS ranges), vendor and product names, whether EUVD lists it as exploited, and a link to the EUVD page; and totals per day and severity (daily_totals, 14 days, complete true only for a whole UTC day). Values are EUVD's, kept as served; the totals are ours. Descriptions and references are not kept. Source: ENISA, EUVD (euvd.enisa.europa.eu); reproduction is authorised if the source is acknowledged. Times are read as UTC. Vulnerabilities in products, never a victim, host or address. A weak signal, not an audit.
